name: envelope-not-exceeded
expectation: ADL business rule EnvelopeNotExceeded: an award commits its amount only by a single conditional write on the call's ledger row that succeeds only if committed + amount <= envelope; otherwise nothing is recorded and the case returns to the chair.

claim.clause: An award commits its amount only by a single conditional write on the call's ledger row that succeeds only if committed + amount <= envelope; otherwise nothing is recorded and the case returns to the chair.

boundary.statement: The call's budget ledger (adj_budget) in the runtime code of the deployable (src/**): every literal SQL write to it, the function holding each write, and every way into that function — a call followed to its HTTP route, or the event whose handler holds the write — in one Quorum process over one store.
includes: UPDATE adj_budget (the commit of an award)
INSERT INTO adj_budget (the ledger row opened when a call is published)
any REPLACE INTO or DELETE FROM adj_budget, were one to exist
every call, in src/**, of the function holding such a write, followed to the route that reaches it

excludes.what: the demo seed's calls of recordDecision (src/seed.ts)
excludes.why: demo data, never run when NODE_ENV=production; it calls the same guarded function

excludes.what: several Quorum processes writing one store at once
excludes.why: one process per store is the deployment model (LocalDevelopment binding). The conditional write and the store's CHECK constraint are the defence there; both are observed statically here, and the implementation's own test tests/scenarios/concurrent-awards.test.ts races separate processes — it is not run by this claim

excludes.what: which amount an award commits (BDL i-q014 AwardIsTheRequestedAmount)
excludes.why: a separate invariant: this claim judges that whatever amount is committed stays within the envelope, not that it equals the requested amount

excludes.what: who may record a decision, on which proposal, and integrity holds (ADL ChairOnScoredOnly)
excludes.why: a separate claim, chair-decides-scored-only; every case here is a chair deciding a scored proposal with no hold

excludes.what: the envelope of the call itself (cal_call.envelope_minor) and its immutability once the call is open
excludes.why: owned by Calls (ADR-006). The ledger copies the envelope once, when CallPublished is delivered; a write that changed adj_budget.envelope_minor afterwards is in scope and would be reported as not admitted

excludes.what: schema DDL (CREATE TABLE adj_budget) in src/platform/schema.ts
excludes.why: defines the ledger, writes no row; its CHECK constraint is observed by store-check-constraint
replaces the database file, not a row of the ledger; an operator act outside the award path

scope.discovery: Lex src/**: every INSERT, REPLACE, UPDATE and DELETE on adj_budget is a write (an UPDATE that sets neither committed_minor nor envelope_minor would not be one; the table has no other value column). The named function holding each write is found. A write inside an event handler of a consumer is entered by that event; otherwise every call of the function in src/** is followed through its own named caller until an HTTP registration, named by method and URL. A call that leads to no route, and non-literal SQL that does not resolve, leave the scope incomplete.
scope.concurrencyStatement: two award requests for different proposals of one call in flight at once, against one process and one store

assumptions.statement: "The call's ledger row" is the adj_budget row keyed by call_id: "committed" is committed_minor and "envelope" is envelope_minor, both integers in minor units (cents). The mapping is stated in scope.table / scope.committed / scope.envelope, not inferred.

The amount an award commits is the proposal's requested amount as the adjudication case holds it (adj_case.requested_minor). The cases choose requested amounts to place committed + amount below, at, one minor unit above and far above the envelope.

"Nothing is recorded" is read as: the ledger's committed amount is unchanged, no adj_decision row exists for the proposal, and no ProposalAwarded is published. The refusal itself is recorded (the case moves to reconsider and AwardRefused is published); that is the case returning to the chair, not a decision.
"The case returns to the chair" is adj_case.status = 'reconsider': the case is still open and undecided, and the chair can still act on it — a further award is refused, a decline is accepted.

Cases set up their world (accounts, a published call, scored proposals) through the implementation's own test harness and services (tests/support/harness.ts), in-process (Fastify inject) against an isolated SQLite file with a manual clock. The acts under test — the decision route and the call publication route — and the state read — adj_budget, adj_decision, adj_case — are the verifier's.

The `reached` paths are what V8 precise BLOCK coverage reports executing during the act alone — the request and the delivery of the events it published; setup excluded. A write is reached when its code ran; a continuation after an early throw is read with the count V8 gives it. Observed by the runtime, not declared.
Writes are found lexically (literal SQL), and the guard checks recognise the code's shape textually (lexed, not parsed); a refactor they do not recognise reads as 'not shown', never as 'violated'.

The concurrent case sends two requests at once to one in-process app. better-sqlite3 runs each write transaction to completion, so the race it can show is between a request's check and its write when the two are not one step — not between two connections or processes.

checks.statement: the writes to the ledger, and the ways into them, are all known: at least one discovered, nothing unresolved

each write to the ledger is either the conditional commit (committed raised by a parameter, on one call's row, only where committed + that amount <= envelope) or the opening of a row at zero that never replaces an existing row; no write changes the committed amount unconditionally, changes the envelope, or deletes or replaces a row
commitAward holds exactly one write: the conditional UPDATE, adding and testing the same amount, and reports the award committed only when that UPDATE changed one row
in recordDecision, an award that was not committed moves the case to reconsider and leaves the function before the decision is recorded
the store itself refuses a ledger row whose committed amount exceeds its envelope (CHECK on adj_budget)
publishing a call through the real route opens its ledger row with the call's envelope and nothing committed
with nothing committed against a 300,000 envelope, the chair awards 100,000 through the real route: exactly that amount is committed and the award is recorded
with 100,000 committed against a 200,000 envelope, an award of exactly 100,000 is admitted: committed equals the envelope, the bound itself is reachable

with 100,000 committed against a 200,000 envelope, an award of 100,000.01 — one minor unit past the envelope — is refused: nothing more is committed, no decision is recorded, no ProposalAwarded is published, and the case returns to the chair. Counts only when its control, award-exactly-fills-envelope, passed on the route

with 150,000 committed against a 200,000 envelope, a further award of 150,000 is refused: nothing more is committed, no decision is recorded, no ProposalAwarded is published, and the case returns to the chair. Counts only when its control, award-within-envelope, passed on the route
a case returned to the chair by a refused award is still the chair's to decide: a second award is refused, a decline is recorded, and the committed amount does not move
with nothing committed against a 200,000 envelope, two awards of 150,000 for different proposals in flight at once: exactly one is admitted and 150,000 is committed

violations.statement: the condition is not enforced on the write: an award is committed although committed + amount exceeds the envelope
the bound is off by one: the comparison admits an award that takes the committed amount one minor unit past the envelope
the check and the write are not one atomic step: two awards in flight both pass the check against the same committed amount and both commit
an award the envelope cannot fund is not refused cleanly: although nothing is committed, the decision is recorded and the case does not return to the chair

challenges.statement: commitAward's UPDATE no longer tests the envelope, and the store's CHECK no longer bounds the committed amount: nothing on the write path keeps committed within the envelope

the bound is one minor unit too generous, in the conditional write and in the store's CHECK (<= envelope + 1): an award far over the envelope is still refused, one a single minor unit over is committed

the route reads whether the award fits, yields, then commits in a transaction that no longer tests the envelope, and the store's CHECK no longer bounds the committed amount: a sequential award over the envelope is still refused, two in flight both commit
recordDecision no longer leaves when the award was not committed: the ledger is untouched, but the award is recorded and published and the case is decided instead of returning to the chair
